questions.question: Why is document chunking critical for RAG system performance?
choices: Smaller chunks always produce better search results
Chunks that are too large dilute relevance scores with irrelevant content, while chunks that are too small lose important context
Chunking is only needed for documents over 10,000 words
The chunk size has no effect on retrieval quality
questions.explanation: Chunk size directly impacts retrieval quality. Oversized chunks include noise that dilutes the relevance signal; undersized chunks miss contextual information needed for meaningful answers. The optimal size balances specificity with context.

questions.question: What is the purpose of overlap in sliding-window chunking?
choices: To make the total number of chunks larger for better coverage
To preserve context across chunk boundaries, ensuring that information split between chunks is still accessible in at least one chunk
To reduce memory usage during embedding generation
Overlap is not recommended in production systems
questions.explanation: Without overlap, a sentence or concept split between two chunks would lose coherence in both. Overlapping windows ensure that content near boundaries appears in multiple chunks, preserving semantic completeness.

questions.question: Which chunking strategy is best for preserving the semantic structure of documents?
choices: Recursive splitting by natural document boundaries (paragraphs, sections, headings) before falling back to smaller units
Putting the entire document into a single chunk
questions.explanation: Recursive/hierarchical chunking respects document structure by splitting on natural boundaries first (sections → paragraphs → sentences). This preserves semantic coherence better than arbitrary fixed-size splits.
